title: Sections over the point commute with scalar extension
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\Ql$ in $\Qlb$ write $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ for the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], for $F=E,L$. For $K\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] put $T_{L/E}K=K\widehat\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, meaning the strict-tower integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], which belongs to $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_L)$ by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]. Let $\Gamma(s,-)$ be sections over the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, applied termwise and passed to derived categories [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. There are isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal O_L)$, natural in $K$,
$$
 \varphi_{L/E,K}:\Gamma(s,T_{L/E}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L.
$$
Here tensor on module complexes is termwise ordinary tensor. The isomorphism is the inverse of the composite of the canonical sections-tensor map with sections of the canonical completion comparison $\chi_{L/E,K}:K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}K$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]; explicitly, if $\theta_{L/E,K}:\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\to\Gamma(s,K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)$ is induced by tensoring sections, then $\varphi_{L/E,K}=(\Gamma(s,\chi_{L/E,K})\circ\theta_{L/E,K})^{-1}$.

For $L=E$ this is the identity under the multiplication and completeness identifications $T_{E/E}K\cong K$. For $E\subset L\subset M$, let $a^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,L,E,K}:T_{M/L}T_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{M/E}K$ be the integral associator obtained by conjugating the ordinary derived-tensor associator $(K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)\otimes^L_{R_L}R_M\cong K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_M$ by the canonical comparisons $\chi$. Write $a^{\mathrm{mod}}$ for the module-complex associator $(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_M\cong N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_M$. Then
$$
 \varphi_{M/E,K}\circ\Gamma(s,a^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,L,E,K})
 =a^{\mathrm{mod}}\circ(\varphi_{L/E,K}\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_M)\circ\varphi_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}.
$$
Tensoring with $L$ over $\mathcal O_L$ gives natural isomorphisms
$$
 \Gamma(s,T_{L/E}K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L\cong
 (\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E)\otimes_E L
$$
in $D(L)$, with the same identity and composition compatibilities.

proof.text: At the geometric point every covering sieve of the final object contains its identity: choose a nonempty weakly etale covering member and use its section over the algebraically closed field. Consequently the sheafification unit is bijective at the final object, for abelian groups and commutative rings. Apply this to the constant finite coefficient rings. Evaluate the completed coefficient tower using jointly injective limit projections and the coefficient-integers profinite-tower isomorphism; this proves that pointCompletedConstant is bijective. Its compatibility with coefficient inclusions follows by applying each finite quotient projection. This identifies completed coefficient sections without identifying the entire completed sheaf with a discrete constant sheaf.

Evaluate the sheafification unit for the change-of-rings presheaf at the final object; the preceding covering argument makes it an isomorphism. Transport along the coefficient-section ring isomorphisms and the specified object/map equations of completedScalarChangeData. This constructs pointSectionsTensor with exactly its pure-tensor normalization. The normalization determines the natural isomorphism uniquely by extendScalars hom-extensionality. Point sections are exact by the existing point-proetale-sections theorem. Integral coefficient extension is flat because the source integers form a principal ideal ring and the target is torsion free; rationalization and field extension are flat by their field structures.

The two chosen ordinary scalar functors have the same coefficient map, objects and morphisms, so identify them and use integralOrdinaryScalar_exact. An exact functor descends to the derived category. Compare this descent with the left-derived functor and universal counit retained by completedScalarChangeData using uniqueness of left derived functors. The factorization equation on every complex is the required normalization, and localization extensionality proves uniqueness. On constructible inputs, identify the two recorded completeness predicates by sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy and apply finiteFreeCompletedScalarComparison, obtaining the specified completion isomorphism. In the legacy interface its auxiliary finite-field datum is arbitrary; construct one of characteristic a prime greater than ell, so no extra hypothesis is imposed on the input.

Obtain the ordinary sheaf unit by evaluating the specified chain multiplication on a degree-zero single complex. Transfer the ordinary sheaf associator from integralOrdinaryScalarComp_existsUnique along equality of the chosen functors, retaining its tensor-section normalization. Use the standard extension-of-scalars unit and associator for coefficient modules. Check the sections unit on 1 tensor n and the sections associativity square on 1 tensor (1 tensor n); adjunction and tensor hom-extensionality show these generators suffice.

Carry the ordinary unit and associativity equations to the exact-functor derived categories. Prove each equality after precomposition with the localization functor and postcomposition with the canonical factorization isomorphisms; naturality of these factorizations reduces it to the ordinary equation degree by degree. Conjugate by the normalized ordinary-to-left-derived comparisons. Finally insert the completion comparisons defining phi and the integral unit/associator. Inverse isomorphism identities and naturality cancel their inner factors. This proves integral naturality, identity and composition with the stated canonical constructions.

Construct the ordinary rationalization comparison as the composite of the two standard extension-of-scalars composition isomorphisms. Its balanced tensor formula determines it uniquely. Check its unit equation on 1 tensor (1 tensor n), and its associativity equation on the corresponding triple tensor. Descend these equations by the same localization-factorization calculation as in the preceding step. Rational phi is the image of integral phi followed by this comparison; its naturality follows from comparison naturality, and its unit and composition equations follow by applying rationalization to their integral counterparts and inserting the two comparison identities.
